subject: Post-call: compute reservation checklist & isolation asks
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Cole <erin.cole@medsync.health>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@medsync.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: compute reservation checklist & isolation asks

Thanks again for your time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a short checklist (redwood-dedicated-checklist.pdf) that captures the items below.

Key pain points you highlighted:
- Latency spikes during peak inference windows (user-facing search and chat flows) causing poor UX at ~p95.
- Regulatory requirement for tenant isolation and auditability for PHI-derived metadata.
- Need predictable throughput for batch and real-time LLM calls during campaign bursts.
- Cost sensitivity: want to avoid significant overprovisioning but need strong SLOs.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Reserved capacity to cover steady-state + controlled burst: target equivalence of ~4 A100 GPUs for inference (estimate based on current qps).
2) Isolation: VPC + tenant segmentation; separate KV caches per tenancy and audit logs retained for 12 months.
3) SLO targets: p95 latency < 250ms for short-turn text generation paths; end-to-end tail < 1s for complex prompts.
4) Procurement window: finalize commercial commitment by end of July so you can align procurement.

Technical constraints we captured:
- Sequence length distribution is skewed (40% short <128 tokens, 60% variable up to 2k).
- Some models must be quantized-compatible (we discussed int8/4 strategies).
- EU data residency not required for initial roll; US region first wave.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Neha: circulate checklist + MP plan (attached) — action: confirm throughput profile during peak demo (you promised sample traces) — ETA: Thu 6/12.
- Erin: share sample request traces and preferred procurement timeline — ETA: Tue 6/17.
- Ben: scope runbook for isolation + ops handoff (isolation-ops-runbook.md) — ETA: Fri 6/13.
- Redwood: propose a two-week technical workshop + mutually agreed MAP (Mutual Action Plan) once traces received.

If anything above is inaccurate or missing, call it out and I’ll update the checklist. Appreciate the clear priorities on your side — we’ll aim to map cost/latency tradeoffs into a recommended reserved-capacity plan.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-checklist.pdf
From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@medsync.health>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@medsync.health>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 13:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: compute reservation checklist & isolation asks

Thanks Neha — this looks good and lines up with our notes. A couple of clarifications: 

- For throughput, the 4x A100 is in the right ballpark but our peak qps during promos could be ~30% higher; I’ll push realistic traces over tomorrow.
- For retention, we need a clear list of what’s stored in the KV cache (we prefer ephemeral where possible).
- Procurement: July timeline is fine but we also want a 30-day pilot window before a long-term commit.

Please loop in the engineering lead for your isolation runbook so we can get into technical weeds.

Thanks,
Erin
Head of Platform Engineering
MedSync Health

Subject: Re: Post-call: compute reservation checklist & isolation asks

Following up from a systems perspective — I sketched an ops/hand-off plan and a few engineering constraints. See isolation-ops-runbook.md (attached). High level notes: 

- Isolation model: recommend single-tenant pools (reserved) for PHI paths + shared multi-tenant pools for non-PHI, enforced via network-level ACLs and separate KV namespaces.
- KV cache: treat as ephemeral by default; durable snapshots only for audit traces — these will be exported to your S3 under customer-controlled keys. Retention policy configurable (default 12 months).
- Autoscaling & burst: propose a staged burst policy — guaranteed baseline (4 GPU equiv), burst to 6 for 4 hours/day during campaigns with pre-warming to avoid first-request cold tails.
- SLO monitoring: p95/p99 token latency, coupling to rollout rules so we can step down model size on tail regressions.

Open questions for MedSync engineers:
1) Preferred auth for export buckets (IAM role vs service account).
2) Any hard constraint on cold-start windows for your user flows (<200ms target?).
3) Which internal teams need read-only access to audit logs?

I’ll stand up a short workshop agenda once we have traces.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: isolation-ops-runbook.md

Appreciate the detailed notes and Ben — the runbook looks reasonable at a glance. We’ll: 
- Share request traces and a sample production SLA by EOD Thu (6/12).
- Confirm auth preference: we prefer customer IAM role for S3 exports.
- Confirm pilot window: 30 days as noted; post-pilot we’ll formalize reserved commit.

Erin
